Chuma Somdaka - Homeless Artist

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
She sleeps on the streets but aspiring artist Chuma Sumdako does not let that stunt her passion or ambitiont

Summary:
Chuma Somdaka is homeless artist, sleeping on a bench in Cape Town's Company Gardens.  She's also a passionate artist who sleeps on top of her creations to keep them safe.  She has also, remarkably, started blogging about her art and what it takes to survive on the streets of the Mother City.

Her name, Chuma Somdaka, means ‘dirty blossom’ in isiXhosa, she’s disabled, from an amputation above the knee you’ll find her on Government Ave in the Company Gardens where she does most of her drawing and sketching.
Her bed a bench in the Company Gardens, to safe keep her art she sleeps on top of it but it’s a struggle to keep them clean. She started a blog in order to share her life experiences as an artist and as a home less woman living on the streets of the city. She does this by using the computers in the Cape Town Library. 

31 years old, she comes from Mthatha in the Eastern Cape hoping that in the mother city there would be more opportunity to create a better life better life. She says creating art up lifts her:
My art has helped me deal with a whole lot of issues. It uplifts me and gives me something positive to look at with the hope that I'll soon be able to get a job and study art.

The Cape Town Public Library also has some of her pictures displayed on their board her first step to success and the realisation of her dream of having her art exhibited in one of the Cape Town galleries.
I have a passion for visual arts and design, and would some day like to be able to study for a degree in the field. Today, I am only thankful that I’m able, through drawing and painting, to have money to use towards my needs.

Press Release:


Sleeping on Her Art
She sleeps on the streets, but aspiring artist Chuma Somdaka doesn’t let that stunt her passion or ambition. This homeless artist, who sleeps on her artwork to keep it safe, has recently become noticed for her unusual blog posts. Chuma Somdaka shares with Carte Blanche what it takes to survive and feed her creativity on the streets.


Script:


LINK
Chuma Somdaka is an artist who uses a stick and pastels to sketch her favourite subject. People and while she has grand ambitions to on day hang her art in a gallery for now her studio’s the Company Gardens in CT.

John: Should I be worried that you saw my hair as purple?
Chuma: Not purple but blue but the colours are more…
John: More subtle I’m a knda subtle personality. You gave me a square head which I am quiet fond of
Laughs

V/O 12 sec
Walking down Government Ave, in Cape Town’s Company Garden’s you’ll find Chuma sitting on her favourite bench, showing her work, her portraits of the people she shares her space with.

V/O 7 sec
And this bench is also where she sleeps every night, her home for the past 2 years.

John: For people that live on the streets it's not that easy is it? You have to take all your worldly possessions every time you move?
Chuma: It takes a lot because you don’t know from day to day where you are going to be, what you are going to eat. So me faith and having the word and using the Bible actually set me free from most things.

Link: Chuma spent her first 27 years in Umtata in the Eastern Cape but she felt compelled to leave. She chose to move to CT where her father lived and where she hoped she could further her education

V/O 20 sec ( If you cant fit it in cut out her age)
But things did not work out, her father died and while Chuma had an internship to learn business administration she couldn’t afford the train fare, she was gang raped and, if things could get any wors, she lost her leg after a hit and run. Two years ago, at 29 years old, Chuma found herself alone and homeless.

Chuma: Not having clothes or toiletries I was ashamed to enter a library or be around people because you tend to smell, so it ended up staying six months in the garden not going out …so that frustration built and this one time I was sitting by the toilets and I picked up a stick because I was frustrated and lit it up with a lighter that I found in the grass . 1st portrait I did was of a girl named MichelIe used to call her my muse.

V/O 7 sec
And that was the start of Chuma’s art….. her portraits of the people she’s met on the streets.

So Chuma is it true that the most difficult feature to draw is the eye
Yea , cause that is the soul to the person
The window to the soul
There’s some sort of connection while you are drawing as well
That’s why most times I use colour not black and white, I feel and think as people theres more colour around us emotions and energy

V/O 11 sec
And then last year Chuma started to blog……which she does from The National Library at the bottom of the gardens she there most days sharing her art, pouring her heart out.

John: Chuma do you think in some ways being homeless and you find yourself in this situation has unlocked this talent inside of you?
Chum: I think in a way its helped me a lot its got me to a place where I can find peace…
Chuma: The streets I wouldn’t recommend that to come and find your self its not the place you come and find your self…it kills a person emotionally.
John: You do our best with the situation but its not a situation you would recommend to other people
Chuma: No, I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone its hell…Hell…Dark dark hell

V/O 14 and a half sec
Last year Chuma, found her self in a dark place she saw no way out of surrounded by drugs and junkies… her fellow homeless people couldn’t understand why she didn’t leave her art and beg …then her life took a small turn.

Link: Sarah Schaeffer a local photographer was jogging down Government Ave when she spotted Chuma’s work on a near by bench Chuma’s use of colour intrigued her so she struck a conversation, that initial interaction is now a budding friendship

Sarah: Its hard not to look twice at her drawings they are colourful and they moving Yea and after seeing her so many times and noticing each other you cant help but start talking and then it grows into something else over time
John: When you First started talking how did she respond to you
Sarah: she is always hesitant with new people so It did take a while , but I what worked with us I engaged with her with her art and we could speak about portraits and I love photographing portraits and she loves drawing people so we had something to connect over.
Chuma: She has helped me a great deal she took me out of a dark place that I was,
the fact she approached me and I didn’t expect that and she actually wanted t a relationship instead of just wanting to buy my art….she’s a beautiful person

John: On a Practical level how have you helped
Sarah: Just very Basic things that make her life easier like doing laundry my flat is nearbyshe stores some things in my garage it seems so so little and minor but it makes things easier for her that’s great I’m happy to help

V/O 16 sec
Sleeping rough, living on the streets, it’s the small practicalities of life that make up your day, things we take for granted. Its in her blog, My Name is Chuma that she feels able to tell her story about being an artist without a home.

Chuma: Blogging some were I could write and I could tell, the blog became somewhere I could let go so ….free myself
Was it difficult to open up
No I thinks I needed to open up I think it was some thing I needed to do…

Sarah: She has a lot to say about her art she thinks very deeply about it she connects with people and that also became clear after meeting some of people she draws she really does have a special connection with them.

John: What are your aspirations what are your hopes for the future?
Chuma: I hope to go to school, to get a qualification and to teach others art because actually heals because most people out on the streets are actually….CRYS…..
John: So you what’s interesting you don’t plan to use your art for selfish reasons but to help other people who are in a similar predicament to you?
Chuma It doesn’t mean everybody will be healed by it it’s a process where they can actually even if its one page….take out and release.

John: I suppose its easy to be utterly heart broken by her story because she’s had one traumatic experience after the next but underlying all that do you think there is something inspirational about her story
Sarah: Absolutely just the fact that’s she can be optimistic and that she does smile when she meets someone and she’s completely inspirational there are so many things in her way and she gets thorough it

LINK: As the Cape Town CBD empties after the working day the cities homeless make there way to where they will be spending the night for Chuma that’s a bench here on Government Ave where a nearby camera offers at least a little security

V/O 22 secs But there are lot of gaps so read each phrase and we will place.

Chuma packs up her pastels, puts her artwork in its folder……

she sleeps on her art to keep it safe…..

She gets out her anorak …

positions her legs around the arm of the bench and covers herself….

For Chuma It’s just another night on the street.
